To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the prevalence of self‐reported LEs was high in a large population‐based sample of CSs, with the most common LEs being fatigue, pain, and sexual problems; 2) CSs with LE reported significantly more problems than those without LE, with the largest differences seen in physical functioning and social functioning, and 3) CSs with self‐reported LE were significantly more likely to report unmet care needs and to utilize health services.
